subject: electronics
title: Sensor divider: darkness switches the lamp on Exit Ticket

questions.prompt: A student says that as it gets darker the voltage across the LDR falls and the lamp switches off. What is the best correction?

choices.text: The student is right - darkness switches the lamp off
As the LDR resistance rises in the dark, its share of the supply rises until it crosses the 4.5 V threshold and switches the lamp on.
The output voltage never changes with light level
The lamp is switched by the fixed resistor alone

questions.misconception: As it gets darker and the LDR's resistance rises, the voltage across the LDR falls, so the sensor output switches the lamp off.
questions.feedback: If you agreed with the student, that is the trap: As it gets darker and the LDR's resistance rises, the voltage across the LDR falls, so the sensor output switches the lamp off. Reteach point: In a series divider each resistor takes a share of the supply in proportion to its resistance, so as the LDR's resistance rises in the dark its share - the output voltage - climbs until it crosses the threshold and switches the lamp on.

questions.prompt: In one sentence, explain why the output voltage rises as the light falls.
questions.answer: The LDR resistance rises as light falls, and each resistor takes a share of the supply in proportion to its resistance, so the LDR share - the output - climbs.
questions.feedback: A strong answer names the share rule: rising resistance means a rising share of the 6 V supply.

questions.prompt: At dusk the output is 4.2 V and the threshold is 4.5 V. What is the state of the lamp?

choices.text: On, because 4.2 V is close to the threshold
Off, because 4.2 V is still below the 4.5 V threshold
Flashing, because the output is near the threshold
On, because dusk is dark enough

questions.feedback: Scene 3 shows dusk: 4.2 V is close to but still below the 4.5 V threshold, so the lamp stays off.

questions.prompt: State the output voltage in the dark and say why the lamp switches on at that stage only.
questions.answer: In the dark the output is 5.4 V, the first value above the 4.5 V threshold, so only then does the sensor output switch the lamp on.
questions.feedback: Credit the threshold reasoning: 5.4 V crosses 4.5 V, while 1.2 V, 3.0 V and 4.2 V all stay below it.
